  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are
not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no
action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
 Youth Commission Regular Meeting Agenda  Page 3 of 3  December 5, 2024

meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The
Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
KManisco@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device
for the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In
compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext.
229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to
ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing
agenda was posted in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 26th day of
November 2024 at 10:00 a.m.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Community Service Learning Opportunities

  Recommended Action: 1) Discuss and approve in-person community service
  learning opportunities from November 2024 and January 2025.

  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou presented the staff report.

  Vice Chair Norby recommended a trail clean-up day.

  Commissioner Myers indicated agreement with Vice Chair Norby.

  Commissioner Barzan stated Leo Carrillo could be considered as a clean-up
  location.

  In response to Vice Chair Norby, Recreation Manager Manisco stated beach clean-
  up days were a separate approved assignment.

  In response to K. Epstein, Recreation Manager Manisco stated staff would research
  the Agoura Animal Care Center volunteer requirements .

  Commissioner K. Epstein suggested writing letters to senior citizens in December.

  Chair L. Epstein recommended cookie decorating with senior citizens.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Commission continued the item to the November 7, 2024
  Regular Meeting.

  B.  Donation-Based Programs
  Recommended Action: Discuss and approve non-profit beneficiaries receiving
  contributions from Youth Commission donation drives in December 2024 and
  February 2025.

  Recreation Coordinator Spiroglou presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Loquet stated the Thanksgiving Baskets canned food drive program,
  which benefited the Boys & Girls Club of Malibu in November 2024, was a great
  community program.

  Chair L. Epstein suggested a toy drive benefiting the Los Angeles County
  Firefighters Foundation for December 2024.

  Commissioner K. Epstein stated the Commission could host a blanket and towel
  donation drive benefiting a local animal shelter.

  Commissioner Loquet requested flyers and digital images for the donation drives
  so Commissioners could share them with Malibu High School teachers and the
  community.

MOTION  Commissioner Barzan moved, and Commissioner K. Epstein seconded a motion to
  schedule a canned food drive benefiting the Boys & Girls Club of Malibu in
  November 2024, a toy drive benefiting the Los Angeles County Firefighters
  Foundation in December 2024, and a blanket and towels donation drive benefiting
  a local animal shelter in January 2025. The question was called, and the motion
  carried 9-0; Commissioners Pollack and Porat absent.

  Halloween Carnival Spooktacular, Breakfast with Santa, Santa Paws, and the

Subject:  Community Service Learning Opportunities (Continued from October
  2, 2024)

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Discuss and approve two bi-monthly in-person community
service learning opportunities.

DISCUSSION: At the June 24, 2024 Regular meeting, Council approved an assignment
for the Youth Commission (Commission) to coordinate bimonthly in-person community
service learning opportunities.

For several years, the Commission organized volunteer opportunities that benefit the
community. From September 2020 through December 2023, the Commission selected
donation-based drives due to the constraints of the Pandemic. In 2024-25, the
Commission will resume in-person community service.

At the October 2, 2024 Special meeting, the Commission discussed a trail clean-up day,
volunteering at the Agoura Animal Care Center, cookie decorating with senior citizens,
and holiday letter writing for senior citizens.

The Commission is asked to discuss and approve two community service learning
opportunities.

Subject:  Youth Government Summit Series

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide feedback on the topics and representatives for the
Youth Government Summit Series.

DISCUSSION: At the June 24, 2024, Regular meeting, the Council approved an
assignment for the Youth Commission (Commission) to host three presentations with
local government agencies and non-profit organization representatives regarding their
career paths and job responsibilities.

Since January 2018, the Commission has organized the Youth Government Summit
(Summit) with local professionals and government officials. In 2023, Ann Buxie, Malibu
Poet Laureate, Gabe Etcheverry, City of Malibu Fire Liaison, and Scott Houston, Director
for the West Basin Municipal Water District, participated in the Summit and focused on
community activism and the importance of teen advocacy in a community.

Historically, the Summit included presentations from three speakers in one session. The
2024-25 Commission expressed interest in having single presentations during Regular
meetings. Previous speakers covered multiple topics, including animal rights activism,
climate change, local government, mental health, and natural disaster preparedness.

The Commission is asked to provide feedback on the topics and representatives for the
Youth Government Summit Series.

Subject:  Youth Commission Mid-Year Activity Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Develop a list of the Commission’s activities for the period
of July through December 2024 to be included in the City Manager’s Mid-Year
Commission Activity Report, scheduled to be presented to the City Council at its Regular
meeting on February 10, 2025.

DISCUSSION: At the June 24, 2024, Regular meeting, the Council approved an
assignment for the Youth Commission (Commission) to provide the City Council with a
mid-year written report on Commission activities (Attachment 1).

The Commission is requested to develop a list of its activities during the first half of the
Fiscal Year, July through December 2024. The City Manager will present the mid-year
report to City Council at its February 10, 2025 Regular meeting. The City Council
requests either the Commission Chair or Vice Chair attend the Regular meeting to
answer questions regarding the report.

Staff has prepared a draft report of the Commission’s completed assignments since July
2024 (Attachment 2). The Commission is asked to review the Draft Mid-Year Report and
provide feedback.

   City of Malibu
  MEMORANDUM

To:  Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission

From:  Steve McClary, City Manager

Date:  June 26, 2024

Re:  Youth Commission Assignments for Fiscal Year 2024-25

At its Regular meeting on June 24, 2024, the City Council approved assignments for the Harry Barovsky
Memorial Youth Commission during Fiscal Year 2024-2025:

  1.  Each Commissioner will volunteer at two City special events; Tiny Tot Olympics, Halloween
  Bu Bash Carnival, Breakfast with Santa, and Chumash Day

  2.  Coordinate bimonthly in-person community service learning opportunities

  3.  Coordinate bimonthly donation-based programs that benefit nonprofit organizations

  4.  Coordinate a community movie night or film screening focusing on teen wellness

  5.  Host three presentations from local government agencies and non-profit organization
  representatives regarding their career path and job responsibilities

  6.  Promote environmental sustainability by hosting a Beach Clean-Up Day

  7.  Develop social media content to promote Voter Registration and participation

  8.  Review opportunities for teen outreach and communication to increase attendance and
  awareness at programs and events

  9.  Review and provide feedback on City projects and programs

  10.  Make bimonthly oral reports as needed to City Council on Commission activity

  11.  Submit a mid-year written report to the City Council on Commission activity
   City of Malibu
  MEMORANDUM

TO:  Mayor Stewart and Honorable Members of the Malibu City Council

FROM:  Chair Logan Epstein and Members of the Youth Commission

DATE:  December 5, 2024

SUBJECT:  Youth Commission Mid-Year Activity Report

As directed by the City Council at its June 24, 2024 Regular meeting, the Youth Commission
submits the following summary of its activities during the first half of Fiscal Year 2024-25
(July through December), approved at the Commission's Regular meeting on December 5,
2024:

    Volunteered twenty hours of community service at city events hosted by the
  Community Services Department, including the Tiny Tot Olympics and the Halloween
  Bu Bash Carnival.

    Hosted a screening of the film, “My Ascension,” on September 30, 2024, focusing on
  suicide prevention and teen wellness. The event was in partnership with the LA
  County Malibu Library Speaker Series and the Boys & Girls Club of Malibu Wellness
  Center.

    Developed and posted social media content to promote Voter Registration and
  participation on Community Services Department platforms, including Facebook and
  Instagram.

    Collected canned food and non-perishable food items on November 3, 2024, to
  benefit the Boys & Girls Club of Malibu, Thanksgiving Baskets Program.
